claims.text: A 60-year-old female presented to the emergency department with right knee pain after a mechanical fall, one month after a right total knee arthroplasty with an unremarkable postoperative course. She had mild swelling, full passive range of motion and could bear weight with assistance. Radiographs showed intact prosthetic components without fracture, loosening or malalignment, and she was discharged with conservative management.

claims.text: Reconstruction used an Achilles tendon allograft with a bone block secured in a tibial trough by a screw, with the tendon branches fixed to the patella, quadriceps tendon and retinacula, and the native tendon stump incorporated. Patellar height and continuity were confirmed intraoperatively and there were no complications. Postoperatively she used an immobilizer, stayed non-weight bearing, and at the clinic visit had improved knee stability and restored active extension without infection, graft failure or wound complications.
